changelog

Changelog

2026-08-22

Fez 0.6 added typed boundaries and native motion

Typed PROPS, element transitions, FLIP reordering, and content-size animation rounded out the 0.6 runtime.

<script>
  class {
    PROPS = {
      message: { type: String, required: true },
      duration: { type: Number, default: 3000 },
      open: { type: Boolean, state: true },
    }

    onMount() {
      if (this.state.open) {
        this.setTimeout(() => {
          this.state.open = false
        }, this.props.duration)
      }
    }
  }
</script>

{#if state.open}
  <aside fez:in="fly, from=right, duration=220" fez:out="fade, duration=140">
    {props.message}
  </aside>
{/if}

<auto-notice message="Saved" duration="1800" open></auto-notice>
2026-08-20

Pjax joined the Fez runtime

Bundling the former dux-pjax package connected server-rendered navigation with Fez's component-aware DOM morphing.

<nav><a href="/account">Account</a></nav>

<main id="content" class="pjax">
  <h1>Account</h1>
  <a href="/account/billing">Billing</a>
</main>

<script>
  class {
    init() {
      this.state.path = location.pathname
    }

    onMount() {
      this.on('pjax:render', (event) => {
        this.state.path = new URL(event.detail.to, location.href).pathname
      })
    }
  }
</script>

<span>Current page: {state.path}</span>
2026-08-10

Style scope became explicit on the tag

Fez removed its CSS-in-JS dependency and made scoped, global, nested, and hoisted CSS behavior part of its own compiler.

<style>
  padding: 16px;
  border: 1px solid var(--line);

  &:hover {
    border-color: #c8102e;
  }

  article {
    display: grid;
    gap: 8px;

    h2 {
      margin: 0;
    }
  }

  @keyframes enter {
    from { opacity: 0; }
    to { opacity: 1; }
  }
</style>

<style global>
  :root {
    --line: #e6e7ea;
  }
</style>

<article><slot /></article>
2026-07-11

Component identity stopped depending on sibling position

Source signatures and explicit keys made component preservation reliable when lists insert, remove, or reorder children.

<!-- account-list.fez -->
<script>
  class {
    init() {
      this.state.accounts = [
        { id: 7, name: 'Personal' },
        { id: 12, name: 'Studio' },
      ]
    }

    reverse() {
      this.state.accounts.reverse()
    }
  }
</script>

<button onclick="fez.reverse()">Reverse</button>

{#each state.accounts as account}
  <account-row key={account.id} :account="account"></account-row>
{/each}

<!-- account-row.fez -->
<script>
  class {
    PROPS = {
      account: { type: Object, required: true },
    }
  }
</script>

<label>
  {props.account.name}
  <input placeholder="Unsaved note" />
</label>
2026-06-04

Events became lifecycle-safe and optionally strict

this.on centralized listener cleanup, and strict event attributes made target-only interactions concise and reliable.

<script>
  class {
    init() {
      this.state.open = false
      this.state.path = location.pathname
    }

    onMount() {
      this.on('pjax:render', (event) => {
        this.state.path = new URL(event.detail.to, location.href).pathname
      })
    }

    open() {
      this.state.open = true
    }

    close() {
      this.state.open = false
    }
  }
</script>

<button onclick="fez.open()">Show current path</button>

{#if state.open}
  <div class="overlay" onclick!="fez.close()">
    <section>
      <p>{state.path}</p>
      <button onclick="fez.close()">Close</button>
    </section>
  </div>
{/if}
2026-04-28

Editor tooling arrived, and slots learned to disappear

VS Code support improved authoring while slot unwrap let semantic wrappers remain exactly where the component design intended.

<script>
  class {
    NAME = 'nav'

    onMount() {
      this.on(this.root, 'click', (event) => {
        const link = event.target.closest('a')
        if (link) this.root.querySelector('.active')?.classList.remove('active')
        link?.classList.add('active')
      })
    }
  }
</script>

<style>
  & {
    display: flex;
    gap: 12px;
  }
</style>

<slot unwrap />

<section-nav aria-label="Account">
  <a href="/profile">Profile</a>
  <a href="/billing">Billing</a>
</section-nav>
2026-03-30

Fez replaced Idiomorph with its own DOM differ

Owning the differ let Fez preserve component identity, slots, refs, and render hashes according to its own lifecycle rules.

<script>
  class {
    init() {
      this.state.count = 0
    }

    increment() {
      this.state.count++
    }

    submit() {
      alert(this.email_input.value)
    }
  }
</script>

<input fez:this="email_input" type="email" placeholder="Type, then increment" />
<button onclick="fez.increment()">Render {state.count}</button>
<button onclick="fez.submit()">Read email</button>
2026-01-30

Await blocks and documentation moved into the component

Promises gained visible loading and error states while info and demo blocks made each .fez file explain and demonstrate itself.

<info>
  <ul>
    <li>Loads one user and renders pending, success, and error states.</li>
    <li>Prop: <code>user_id</code>.</li>
  </ul>
</info>

<demo>
  <user-summary user_id="42"></user-summary>
</demo>

<script>
  class {
    PROPS = {
      user_id: { type: Number, required: true },
    }

    init(props) {
      this.state.user = Fez.fetch(`/api/users/${props.user_id}`)
    }
  }
</script>

{#await state.user}
  <p>Loading user...</p>
{:then user}
  <h2>{user.name}</h2>
  <p>{user.email}</p>
{:catch error}
  <p>Could not load user: {error.message}</p>
{/await}
2026-01-22

Fez adopted Svelte-like templates without adopting Svelte

A familiar block syntax improved readability while Fez kept its own compiler, runtime, and DOM ownership model.

<script>
  class {
    init() {
      this.state.selected = 2
      this.state.people = [
        { id: 1, name: 'Ada' },
        { id: 2, name: 'Grace' },
      ]
    }

    select(id) {
      this.state.selected = id
    }
  }
</script>

{#if state.people}
  <ul>
    {#each state.people as person}
      <li class:selected={person.id === state.selected}>
        <button onclick="fez.select({person.id})">{person.name}</button>
      </li>
    {/each}
  </ul>
{:else}
  <p>No people found.</p>
{/if}
2026-01-20

The CLI started validating the component format

Compile and refactor commands turned Fez's browser compiler knowledge into dependable local and CI feedback.

fez compile ./demo/fez/ui-dialog.fez
fez template ./demo/fez/ui-dialog.fez

fez compile './demo/fez/**/*.fez'
fez refactor ./demo/fez

fez compile --debug-template ./demo/fez/ui-dialog.fez
fez template --debug ./demo/fez/ui-dialog.fez
2025-09-11

Shared state stayed observable and debuggable

Global pub/sub, state subscriptions, dump helpers, and CSS mixins expanded coordination without hiding it behind a store framework.

<!-- theme-toggle.fez -->
<script>
  class {
    init() {
      this.state.dark = Boolean(Fez.state.get('dark'))
    }

    toggle() {
      this.state.dark = !this.state.dark
      Fez.state.set('dark', this.state.dark)
      document.documentElement.classList.toggle('dark', this.state.dark)
    }
  }
</script>

<button onclick="fez.toggle()">
  Use {state.dark ? 'light' : 'dark'} theme
</button>

<theme-toggle></theme-toggle>
<p>Dark mode: <fez-inline>{globalState.dark ? 'on' : 'off'}</fez-inline></p>

<script>
  Fez.state.subscribe('dark', (value, oldValue) => {
    console.log('dark changed', { oldValue, value })
  })
</script>
2025-08-05

fez:keep made preservation explicit

A stable preservation key gave expensive or stateful DOM subtrees a clear contract with the renderer.

<script>
  import Chart from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/chart.js@4/+esm'

  class {
    init() {
      this.state.title = 'Revenue'
    }

    onMount() {
      this.local.chart = new Chart(this.chart_node, {
        type: 'line',
        data: this.props.data,
      })
    }

    onDestroy() {
      this.local.chart?.destroy()
    }
  }
</script>

<h2>{state.title}</h2>
<div fez:keep="revenue-chart" fez:this="chart_node"></div>
2025-08-01

The Fez toolchain became native Bun

Removing the Ruby builder and publishing the package made compilation and indexing available from one JavaScript toolchain.

bun ./bin/fez compile ./demo/fez/ui-counter.fez
bun ./bin/fez template ./demo/fez/ui-counter.fez
bun ./bin/fez refactor ./demo/fez

bun add @dinoreic/fez
bunx --package @dinoreic/fez fez compile './components/**/*.fez'
2025-07-27

ES modules moved inside the component file

Module-context imports let a .fez file declare external behavior without a second bootstrap script.

<script>
  Fez.head({
    importmap: {
      'date-fns': 'https://esm.sh/date-fns@4',
    },
  })

  import { formatDistanceToNow } from 'date-fns'

  class {
    PROPS = {
      since: { type: Date, required: true },
    }

    init() {
      this.state.distance = ''
    }

    beforeRender() {
      this.state.distance = formatDistanceToNow(this.props.since, {
        addSuffix: true,
      })
    }
  }
</script>

<time datetime={props.since.toISOString()}>{state.distance}</time>

<relative-time since="2025-07-27T12:00:00Z"></relative-time>
2025-07-23

Global components and Fez.fetch covered page-level services

Singleton components and a cached request helper made dialogs, data panels, and other page-level services straightforward.

<script>
  class {
    GLOBAL = 'BuildStatus'

    init() {
      this.state.build = Fez.fetch('/api/build-status')
    }

    reload() {
      Fez.clearFetchCache()
      this.state.build = Fez.fetch('/api/build-status')
    }
  }
</script>

{#await state.build}
  <p>Checking build...</p>
{:then build}
  <p>Build {build.id}: {build.status}</p>
{:catch error}
  <p>Could not load status: {error.message}</p>
{/await}

<button onclick="fez.reload()">Reload</button>
2025-07-15

State, props, and init became the component vocabulary

Fez simplified template access and settled on init as the lifecycle entry point for instance state.

<script>
  class {
    PROPS = {
      label: { type: String, default: 'Count' },
      start: { type: Number, default: 0 },
    }

    init(props) {
      this.state.count = props.start
    }

    increment() {
      this.state.count++
    }
  }
</script>

<button onclick="fez.increment()">
  {props.label}: {state.count}
</button>

<score-counter label="Points" start="10"></score-counter>
2025-06-26

Unless understands empty collections

Fez added a practical empty-state block whose truthiness rules match the way interface data is actually shaped.

<script>
  class {
    init() {
      this.state.notifications = []
    }

    add() {
      this.state.notifications.push({
        id: Date.now(),
        text: 'Build completed',
      })
    }
  }
</script>

<button onclick="fez.add()">Add notification</button>

{#unless state.notifications}
  <p>You are all caught up.</p>
{/unless}

{#each state.notifications as notification}
  <p key={notification.id}>{notification.text}</p>
{/each}
2025-06-19

A Fez component became loadable by URL

URL loading made a .fez file a portable component artifact that a page can consume without a local build pipeline.

<script src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dux/fez/main/dist/fez.js"></script>

<script fez="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dux/fez/main/demo/fez/ui-counter.fez"></script>

<ui-counter start="2"></ui-counter>
2025-01-31

A component can declare what it needs in the document head

Fez.head made external CSS, scripts, and import maps part of the component module instead of hidden page setup.

<script>
  Fez.head({
    importmap: {
      'nanoid': 'https://esm.sh/nanoid@5',
    },
  })

  Fez.head({
    css: 'https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/font-awesome/6.5.1/css/all.min.css',
  })

  import { nanoid } from 'nanoid'

  class {
    init() {
      this.state.document_id = nanoid()
    }
  }
</script>

<p><i class="fa-solid fa-file"></i> Document: <code>{state.document_id}</code></p>
2025-01-25

Fez began owning its template compiler

Replacing the early renderer gave Fez control over template semantics, errors, and the cost of each render.

<script>
  class {
    init() {
      this.state.filter = 'all'
      this.state.visible = []
      this.state.tasks = [
        { id: 1, title: 'Compile template', done: true },
        { id: 2, title: 'Morph DOM', done: false },
      ]
    }

    beforeRender() {
      this.state.visible = this.state.filter === 'all'
        ? this.state.tasks
        : this.state.tasks.filter(task => task.done)
    }
  }
</script>

{#if state.visible.length}
  <ul>
    {#each state.visible as task}
      <li key={task.id}>{task.title}</li>
    {/each}
  </ul>
{:else}
  <p>No matching tasks.</p>
{/if}
2024-07-17

Components needed local styles and durable slots

Style scoping, slot preservation, and binding work turned isolated demos into components that could live safely on real pages.

<!-- info-panel.fez -->
<script>
  class {
    init() {
      this.state.open = true
    }

    toggle() {
      this.state.open = !this.state.open
    }
  }
</script>

<style>
  section {
    border: 1px solid #d2d4d9;
    border-radius: 10px;
    padding: 16px;

    button {
      margin-bottom: 10px;
    }
  }
</style>

<section>
  <button onclick="fez.toggle()">Toggle details</button>
  {#if state.open}
    <slot />
  {/if}
</section>

<info-panel>
  <p>This paragraph belongs to the page that uses the component.</p>
</info-panel>
2024-07-14

Pub/sub made components cooperate without coupling

The first substantial demos arrived with a small event model for communication within and across component trees.

<!-- add-to-cart.fez -->
<script>
  class {
    add() {
      Fez.publish('cart:add', { id: this.props.product_id })
    }
  }
</script>

<button onclick="fez.add()">Add to cart</button>

<!-- cart-count.fez -->
<script>
  class {
    init() {
      this.state.count = 0
      this.subscribe('cart:add', () => {
        this.state.count++
      })
    }
  }
</script>

<span>Cart: {state.count}</span>

<add-to-cart product_id="book-7"></add-to-cart>
<cart-count></cart-count>
2024-07-11

Templates escape HTML unless I explicitly opt out

Escaped interpolation became the safe default, with a visible raw-HTML directive for trusted content.

<script>
  class {
    init() {
      this.state.user_text = '<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>'
      this.state.trusted_html = '<strong>Saved successfully.</strong>'
    }
  }
</script>

<p>User input: {state.user_text}</p>
<div class="notice">{@html state.trusted_html}</div>
2024-07-08

Rendering became component-aware DOM morphing

Fez moved from replacing HTML to morphing it, preserving useful browser and component state across renders.

<script>
  class {
    init() {
      this.state.next_id = 3
      this.state.items = [
        { id: 1, name: 'HTML' },
        { id: 2, name: 'DOM' },
      ]
    }

    add() {
      this.state.items.push({
        id: this.state.next_id,
        name: `Item ${this.state.next_id}`,
      })
      this.state.next_id++
    }
  }
</script>

<button onclick="fez.add()">Add item</button>
<ul>
  {#each state.items as item}
    <li key={item.id}>{item.name}</li>
  {/each}
</ul>
2024-07-01

Reactivity needs a direct route back to the DOM

Reactive state and fez:this arrived together because useful components need both declarative rendering and precise DOM access.

<script>
  class {
    init() {
      this.state.message = ''
    }

    onMount() {
      this.name_input.focus()
    }

    greet() {
      const name = this.name_input.value.trim()
      this.state.message = name ? `Hello, ${name}.` : 'Please enter a name.'
    }
  }
</script>

<label>
  Name
  <input fez:this="name_input" autocomplete="name" />
</label>
<button onclick="fez.greet()">Greet</button>
<p>{state.message}</p>
2024-06-14

CDE became Fez

Renaming the project clarified that it was a small component layer for real pages, not another abstract element system.

<!-- ./status-pill.fez -->
<script>
  class {
    PROPS = {
      state: { type: String, default: 'pending' },
    }
  }
</script>

<style>
  span {
    display: inline-flex;
    padding: 4px 10px;
    border-radius: 999px;
    background: #f4d9de;
    color: #8e0b21;
  }
</style>

<span>{props.state}</span>

<script fez="./status-pill.fez"></script>

<p>Invoice <status-pill state="paid"></status-pill></p>
2024-06-10

Fez started with the DOM

The first version established the rule that still matters most: enhance the page the server rendered instead of taking it over.

<script src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dux/fez/main/dist/fez.js"></script>
<script fez="./hello-counter.fez"></script>

<h1>Server-rendered account page</h1>
<hello-counter></hello-counter>

<script>
  class {
    init() {
      this.state.count = 0
    }

    increment() {
      this.state.count++
    }
  }
</script>

<button onclick="fez.increment()">Count: {state.count}</button>
